tasks.short: Collect project updates, explain progress and risks, and publish status reports.

steps.what: Chase missing progress updates from workstream leads.
Collect milestone, issue, spending and commitment records.
Reconcile reporting dates, project identifiers and conflicting figures.
Discuss slippage, dependencies and recovery options with workstream leads.
Draft the status report with trends, risks and requested decisions.

loop.input: Validated metrics, dated project updates, decision log and report template.
loop.output: Draft narrative with source references; tables and numeric trends rendered deterministically.
loop.check: Check numeric statements against metrics, require source references and flag unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt per report; fall back to tables and source excerpts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle figures, but explanations and requested decisions depend on free-text updates.

steps.what: Check the report and approve its overall status and escalation wording.
Distribute the approved report to its agreed internal audience.

tasks.design: Configure update reminders and report approvals in the {PROJECT}, then join dated records from the {PROJECT}, {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} through the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Deterministic checks feed a {BI} view and report tables; a bounded loop drafts explanations into the {DOCS}. The project manager approves the report before the {WORKFLOW} distributes it through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reporting dates and identifiers differ across systems. Explaining delays still requires conversations, which made the whole report look unsuitable for automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting features can handle reminders and approvals. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building joins, checks and templates; a small model loop can draft from supplied evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Progress estimates can be optimistic or stale. Unrecorded dependencies and politically sensitive escalations still need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager tests whether a recovery promise is credible and decides how clearly to escalate bad news.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly recovery decisions for critical-path slippage.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to investigating dependencies and resolving recovery choices. Formal decision rights stay unchanged; existing escalation authority can be used sooner.

reach.task: Compare recurring causes of project delay across the portfolio.
reach.learn: Learn consistent delay categories and how to distinguish correlation from a causal explanation.

evidence.claim: Scheduled joins, validation rules and report templates can automate structured reporting preparation.
GitHub Copilot offers coding and review assistance with expected oversight; this supports building integrations, not a measured reporting gain.
An early-2025 experiment with 16 developers found slower completion with AI; it does not establish current build speed for this workflow.

assumptions: This baseline uses a recurring report assembled from system records, a reconciliation workbook and workstream updates.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Existing reporting features are checked before custom components are built.
The design reports project progress rather than scoring individual employees.
unknowns: Which reporting, reminder and approval features are already licensed?
Are project identifiers consistent across financial and delivery records?
Who approves reports containing sensitive commercial or employee information?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the proposed reporting data?
What access, retention and lawful-processing arrangements apply under GDPR?
research_questions: Can built-in reports cover the required fields and reporting cut-off?
How much reconciliation work remains after identifier and date checks?
Does a source-linked narrative reduce review time without hiding uncertainty?
new_work: Review narrative accuracy and escalation wording.
Resolve missing records and inconsistent identifiers.
Maintain metric definitions, connectors and report templates.
Monitor failed distributions and access changes.

tasks.short: Define supplier needs, compare proposals, test suitability and secure selection approval.

steps.what: Write project needs, selection criteria and proposal requirements.
Approve sourcing scope, selection criteria and spending envelope.
Find eligible suppliers using approved supplier records and prior engagements.
Invite shortlisted suppliers to submit proposals.
Register received proposals and identify missing attachments.
Extract and compare scope, costs, exclusions and delivery evidence.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and the approved comparison fields.
loop.output: Evidence grid with source locations, exclusions and unknown fields; totals calculated deterministically.
loop.check: Require source locations, verify currencies and totals, and review material scope differences.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per proposal; unresolved fields remain unknown for manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scope, exclusions and evidence appear in differently worded documents rather than consistent fields.

steps.what: Test delivery claims through demonstrations, references and technical discussions.
Weight trade-offs and recommend a supplier with documented reasons.
Approve the supplier selection under delegated procurement authority.

tasks.design: Configure a sourcing record and approval flow in the {PROCUREMENT}, with proposal documents in the {DOCS} and controlled invitations through the {EMAIL}. A template generator prepares the brief, while a bounded extraction loop builds a source-linked evidence grid and deterministic code checks costs. People conduct demonstrations, recommend the supplier and approve selection before contracting starts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier records were available, but proposals differed in structure and wording. Suitability depended on delivery credibility and technical discussions.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured sourcing records handle tracking and approvals. Bounded extraction can prepare a comparison without delegating the supplier decision.
tasks.still_hard: Omitted costs, weak references and ambiguous scope can survive document checks. Procurement thresholds, security requirements and contract terms vary.
tasks.human_edge: People challenge supplier claims, assess working relationships and accept the trade-offs between price, capability and delivery risk.

ambition.what: Departmental teams buying small IT consulting engagements.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into registering proposals and copying comparison fields. The project manager can support smaller buying teams; supplier approval rights remain with the authorised procurement role.

reach.learn: Learn required supplier checks, approval thresholds and the handoff from selection to contract.

evidence.claim: Sourcing records, invitation templates and approval workflows can reduce administrative work while retaining human selection.
SharePoint autofill columns supports prompt-based document metadata extraction and warns about incorrect results; this is not evidence of supplier-selection quality.

assumptions: The baseline uses approved supplier records plus document proposals and human assessments.
Time shares are estimates; judgement and supplier conversations remain substantial.
The procurement manager represents the authorised selection approver; local delegation may require another role.
Contract negotiation and purchase-order release are separate downstream actions.
unknowns: Which sourcing features and supplier records already exist?
Who may invite suppliers and approve each spending band?
Which technical, security and financial checks are mandatory?
May confidential proposals be processed by the selected model service?
Do consultant-selection criteria assess individuals in ways relevant to GDPR, the EU AI Act or national rules?
research_questions: Can proposals be collected through a standard form before using document extraction?
Which comparison fields are reliable enough for automatic checks?
How often do extraction errors change the apparent ranking?
new_work: Review extracted scope, exclusions and commercial figures.
Maintain comparison fields and invitation templates.
Handle missing proposals, unclear terms and unsupported supplier claims.
Keep confidential proposal access and retention current.

tasks.short: Build annual IT project budgets, agree funding priorities and monitor spending against forecasts.

steps.what: Collect prior spending, current commitments and approved project baselines.
Reconcile project codes, commitments, accruals and cost categories.
Agree effort estimates, delivery assumptions and resource needs with technical leads.
Calculate annual funding scenarios, contingency and forecast completion costs.
Negotiate priorities, scope and contingency with finance and the project sponsor.
Approve the annual budget and authorised spending limits.
Compare monthly actuals and commitments with the approved budget.
Investigate material variances and agree forecast revisions or funding requests.

tasks.design: Join project actuals and commitments from the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT} with delivery baselines from the {PROJECT}. A deterministic scenario generator stores versioned assumptions and forecasts in the {WORKFLOW}, while configured reports expose variances. Budget approval stays in the {ERP}; funding changes return to the authorised approver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Financial records and delivery estimates used different codes and cut-offs. Spreadsheets mixed calculations with uncertain assumptions and negotiated funding choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned records, tested calculations and standard approval features can replace workbook handling. AI-assisted coding can make a small scenario tool economical without using a model for financial arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Effort forecasts, accrual timing and incomplete commitments remain uncertain. Funding trade-offs and accounting treatment need finance involvement.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager challenges estimates, distinguishes temporary variance from structural overspend and negotiates realistic scope.

ambition.what: Weekly forecast revision for projects approaching their approved spending limit.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts towards testing cost assumptions and discussing emerging funding choices. Forecast recommendations become more frequent; authority to approve spending stays unchanged.

reach.task: Compare project funding scenarios with expected operational benefits.
reach.learn: Learn benefit assumptions, sensitivity analysis and the difference between committed and avoidable costs.

evidence.claim: Structured cost reconciliation, scenario arithmetic and variance reporting can use deterministic technology.
GitHub Copilot supports assisted coding and review; the digest provides no documented case of this project-budget workflow.

assumptions: The baseline combines financial system records, scenario workbooks and funding discussions.
Time shares are estimates; reducing preparation does not remove budget judgement.
Configured financial reports can cover recurring variance calculations.
Forecast revisions do not authorise additional spending.
Cost views avoid exposing individual compensation unless necessary and authorised.
unknowns: Are commitments and accruals available by project identifier?
Which cost categories and accounting treatments does finance require?
Who approves annual budgets, contingency release and funding changes?
Which forecasting features are already available?
Do detailed labour-cost views require consultation under national rules?
Which GDPR controls apply to personal data in resource and cost records?
research_questions: Can existing financial planning features cover versioned scenarios?
How much variance comes from timing rather than changed delivery cost?
Do weekly forecast reviews identify actionable changes before the monthly close?
new_work: Resolve unmapped costs and incomplete commitments.
Maintain cost mappings, calculation rules and scenario templates.
Review changed assumptions and unusual forecast movements.
Keep approval limits and financial access current.

tasks.short: Agree project audiences, channels and cadence, then deliver updates and handle stakeholder concerns.

steps.what: Discuss information needs and sensitivities with business and technical leads.
Record audiences, channels, cadence and escalation routes.
Approve the communication plan and sensitive-message approval routes.
Schedule meetings and routine milestone notifications.
Write tailored updates from current project evidence.

loop.input: Approved report, decision log, audience-specific disclosure rules and message template.
loop.output: Audience-specific drafts with source references and proposed recipient groups.
loop.check: Check facts against sources, enforce allowed fields and validate recipients against the approved plan.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair per audience; fall back to an approved template with factual fields.
loop.why_not_simpler: Different audiences need different explanations of the same free-text decisions and risks.

steps.what: Approve update wording and check restricted recipients.
Send approved updates and authorised routine reminders.
Handle stakeholder concerns and agree follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Store audience groups, cadence and approval routes in the {PROJECT}, and configure scheduling through the {CALENDAR} and {WORKFLOW}. A bounded loop prepares tailored drafts in the {DOCS} from approved project evidence. Approval binds the wording and recipients before the {EMAIL} or {CHAT} sends updates; sensitive messages follow the sponsor route.
tasks.previous_blocker: Communication plans were static documents, while recipients and project facts changed. Tailoring messages and handling concerns were mixed with scheduling and distribution.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured schedules and approval records handle routine coordination. A bounded drafting loop can reuse approved evidence for several audiences without generating new commitments.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may distrust accurate updates or need difficult conversations. Recipient changes, confidentiality and implied commitments require careful review.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager recognises concerns, chooses the right moment to communicate and negotiates understanding across technical and business groups.

ambition.what: Frontline operational teams affected by IT project changes.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into calendars, copying facts and distributing updates, leaving more time for affected teams. Communication approval remains delegated as before; sensitive commitments still need sponsor approval.

reach.task: Coordinate sponsor meetings and decision follow-ups.
reach.learn: Learn decision deadlines, confidentiality needs and how to turn meeting outcomes into tracked actions.

evidence.claim: Configured schedules, audience records and approval-bound notifications can reduce communication administration.
TOPdesk summarises tickets and drafts knowledge items for review; this supports the bounded drafting pattern, not proven project-communication gains.

assumptions: The baseline includes internal stakeholders and some external delivery partners.
Time shares are estimates; relationship work remains substantial.
Distribution uses the exact approved content and recipient list; changes invalidate approval.
Routine reminders use templates and audiences authorised in the communication plan.
The design does not infer employee sentiment, record meetings or rate staff.
Build estimates cover a modest first rollout and access setup; required national consultation can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which audiences need updates, and who maintains their membership?
Which messages require sponsor, legal or security approval?
Which scheduling and approval features already exist?
What GDPR retention and access arrangements apply to stakeholder records?
Does the proposed use require consultation under national rules?
Would later interactive features trigger EU AI Act disclosure or employment-related requirements?
research_questions: Which updates can use fixed templates without a model?
Can existing group permissions prevent restricted information reaching the wrong audience?
Do tailored updates improve stakeholder understanding and reduce clarification requests?
new_work: Review draft wording, disclosures and recipients.
Maintain audience groups, cadence and sensitive-message routes.
Handle failed delivery and stakeholder corrections.
Update templates and check the drafting loop against changed project terminology.

role.altitude: The project manager spends less time moving records between systems and more time challenging estimates, resolving dependencies and aligning people. Budget, supplier and sensitive-communication authority remains with existing approvers unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Management analyst: compare delay patterns, costs and expected benefits across projects.
Administrative services manager: improve the supplier-selection-to-onboarding handoff.
Executive administrative assistant: connect sponsor decisions with scheduled follow-up.
Computer systems analyst: translate business constraints into testable delivery requirements.
skills_to_grow: Define consistent project, cost and reporting identifiers.
Design approval gates that bind content, recipients and spending authority.
Review source-linked model drafts and recognise unsupported claims.
Test financial scenarios and challenge delivery assumptions.
Facilitate supplier, sponsor and stakeholder conversations.
Understand GDPR, relevant EU AI Act uses and applicable national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a lightweight project decision service for smaller departmental initiatives: current delivery evidence, cost scenarios, supplier comparisons and audience-specific updates, with named human approvers.
